current_bottleneck: Scalar sample temperature is not a safe risk layer for the native joint AR law. It slightly increases aggregate coverage but leaves persistent sparse-window undercoverage and regime layer2 essentially unchanged, while damaging cointegration, median bias, level KS, cross-cell rank, or per-cell jump-tail structure.
last_result_summary: 611a added --sample_temperature to the 609/610 evaluator and tested 610a at temperatures 1.05 and 1.15 on the full 441-window IV bridge. Baseline 1.00 scored 5/11 with cov90 75.7%. Temp 1.05 scored 4/11: cov90 76.9%, conditional MAE reduction 6.0%, turb/calm width 1.023, daily KS 23/25, level KS 2/25, median-bias cells 9/25, cointegration worst-cell failed at 0.200, pathwise still passed. Temp 1.15 scored 4/11: cov90 78.6%, conditional MAE reduction 4.1%, turb/calm width 1.019, daily KS 22/25, level KS 1/25, per-cell q99 jump-scale fell to 12/25 and pathwise failed. Persistent severe undercoverage stayed about 10.7-10.9%.
next_step_recommendation: Close scalar temperature. Implement a learned conditional source-scale mechanism inside the same generic AR transition model. It should infer positive per-variable noise scale from causal memory state and apply it during both training and sampling, preserving the IV-only/joint38 shared architecture.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
